candidate.title: mNET-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina mNET-Seq schematic, interpreted as the MNase-based mammalian native elongating transcript sequencing implementation described by Nojima et al. The single route starts with native chromatin-associated Pol II–nascent RNA complexes and ends at cDNA. The far-left Cap-labelled icon illustrates the same starting biology, not another workflow. Chromatin fractionation is preparation history of the starting state; adapter preparation and eventual sequencing clarify the library interface/readout but are not separate depicted operations. No alternative target method is shown.

states.label: Native chromatin-associated Pol II–nascent RNA complex
features: Starting preparation: endogenous elongating Pol II complexes in a native mammalian chromatin fraction; fractionation is described in the sources but not drawn as an operation.
Main starting icon: blue Pol II oval on a blue DNA line with emerging purple RNA and a black terminal square labelled m7G. The introductory icon repeats this with the label Cap.
The RNA biological target includes nascent RNA whose native 3′ OH terminal nucleotide lies in the Pol II active site; the drawn capped upstream RNA is not the eventual whole sequenced molecule.

states.label: Soluble MNase-digested chromatin containing Pol II–protected RNA fragments
features: Pol II complexes released into a soluble chromatin fraction retain protein-protected RNA while exposed DNA and RNA are digested.
The panel shows short blue fragments and a separated capped purple RNA segment above the Pol II complex. These are digestion products, not an alternative retained library branch.
The exposed retained RNA end marked OH is the MNase-generated 5′ OH; its Pol II-associated native 3′ OH remains protected. Other protein-protected processing intermediates can also survive.

states.label: cDNA representing the selected RNA fragments

operations.label: MNase digestion
operations.description: Digest exposed chromatin DNA and exposed RNA, releasing Pol II elongation complexes into soluble chromatin and shortening their accessible RNA to protein-protected fragments. The output includes the separated capped upstream RNA and blue digestion fragments shown beside the retained complexes.
operations.mechanism: Micrococcal nuclease attacks accessible nucleic acid; Pol II and associated protein complexes protect retained RNA segments. The drawn orange symbols belong to the digestion panel and are not a separate material branch.
operations.information_effect: The retained RNA 3′ endpoint can preserve the last nucleotide synthesized by Pol II, while upstream accessible RNA and cap continuity are lost. Survival of digestion is a protection-based selection and can include RNA protected by associated processing complexes; it does not establish that every retained RNA end is an active-site end.

operations.label: Immunoprecipitate with Pol II Ab
operations.description: Capture Pol II protein complexes and their associated protected RNA from the soluble digest onto the antibody support. Unbound digestion fragments are not followed into the depicted retained route.
operations.mechanism: Pol II-specific antibody immunoprecipitation retains endogenous polymerase and co-associated RNA. The generic icon leaves the antibody specificity open; primary implementations use antibodies with distinct Pol II/CTD specificities.
operations.information_effect: Introduces an antibody-defined Pol II association for the RNA sample and can enrich particular CTD modification states. RNA processing intermediates tethered through Pol II-associated complexes can remain in the captured material, limiting active-site specificity.

operations.label: 5′ phosphorylation with PNK
operations.description: On the captured complexes, convert the MNase-generated RNA 5′ OH to 5′ phosphate; the drawing changes the exposed RNA-end label from OH to P while keeping Pol II on the antibody support.
operations.mechanism: T4 polynucleotide kinase phosphorylates RNA 5′ ends on the IP beads and leaves the protected Pol II-embedded 3′ OH intact.

operations.label: Purify and size select
operations.description: Recover RNA from the captured complexes, removing DNA and proteins, and retain the RNA size fraction used for library construction. The primary implementation resolves this broad depicted block as selection of 35–100-nt RNA.
operations.mechanism: RNA purification followed by size selection; the paper identifies denaturing-gel recovery of the selected RNA fraction. Routine extraction conditions are outside the schematic scope.
operations.information_effect: Removes the physical Pol II attachment while preserving RNA sequence and end identity plus sample provenance from the antibody selection. Selecting longer protected fragments supports genomic mapping but excludes RNAs below the selected lower bound; it does not separate active-site RNA from all processing-derived RNA.

operations.label: Reverse transcription
operations.description: Copy the selected RNA into the cDNA endpoint drawn at the right. The primary implementation supplies adapter-ligated RNA to reverse transcription; the schematic compresses that unshown interface rather than depicting individual ligation reactions.
operations.mechanism: RNA-dependent DNA synthesis using the selected RNA as template. Strand-specific RNA adapters are reported between RNA purification and reverse transcription, but their internal preparation is not expanded into graph operations.
operations.information_effect: Transfers selected RNA sequence/end information to a DNA carrier for the reported sequencing library. Directional readout of RNA insert 3′ ends supports single-nucleotide genomic profiles of nascent transcription and co-transcriptional cleavage associated with the captured Pol II population. Individual peaks can reflect either Pol II accumulation or protected processing intermediates; the native endpoint cannot invariably be interpreted as Pol II pausing. Sequencing and mapping are explanatory readout context, not additional operations drawn in this image.

method_scopes.rationale: The card heading, collection-page heading/caption and image identify one target: mNET-Seq, also written mNET-seq and expanded as mammalian native elongating transcript sequencing. All five local operations apply to this depicted MNase/Pol II IP implementation. The 2015 full text describes it and the 2016 full-text protocol supplies the same core route. The generic Pol II Ab icon does not fix a particular CTD antibody. TruSeq Small RNA library preparation is an embedded library component, not another target method. Other assays discussed in the papers do not enlarge the image scope.
